B0100.d: B0100 is the general fault for air blower A in a sensor cleaning system, i.e. the fan or motor unit itself rather than its wiring or relay (those are B0102 and B0104).
s: Sensor blocked or cleaning fault message
Driver assistance or automated driving functions limited or switched off
No airflow audible or felt at the sensor outlets
c: Blower A motor worn, seized or with an open winding
Impeller blocked by ice, leaves or debris in the intake duct
Corroded or loose plug directly at blower A

B0101.d: B0101 reports a fault of the second cleaning air source, blower B. A second unit makes sense where sensors are spread over the body: a roof pod and a bumper or corner sensor need separate air supplies.
s: Cleaning fault shown for the sensor group served by blower B
Water droplets or dust remain on lidar or camera window
Assistance functions reduced when the affected sensor goes blind
c: Blower or compressor B worn out or drawing too much current
Leaking or split air hose so blower B cannot build pressure
Water or salt ingress into blower B at an exposed mounting point

B0102.d: B0102 narrows the blower A problem down to its control path: the controlling module sees a wrong voltage or current on the line that commands blower A, typically an open circuit, a short to ground or a short to supply. In Ford's lidar cleaning patent US10569746B2 a computer opens airflow from a blower or compressor by driving an electric solenoid valve and may modulate it; when window opacity exceeds about 30 %, air
s: Blower A never starts although cleaning is requested
Blower A runs constantly when the line is shorted to supply
Sensor blocked message and limited assistance features
c: Broken control wire or pin between module and blower A
Control line of blower A shorted to ground or to battery voltage
Output stage in the cleaning or maintenance module defective

B0103.d: With B0103 the module flags the command line of blower B, not the blower: open wire, short or a driver that cannot switch. In compressed-air layouts the controlled element is often a valve bank.
s: Lens streaks or droplets remain after a wash cycle
Cleaning warning for sensors on the B circuit only
Assistance features temporarily unavailable in rain or dust
c: Damaged harness or connector in the control path of blower B
Solenoid coil of the B air valve open or shorted, where air is valve-switched
Failed driver for blower B in the controlling module

B0104.d: B0104 points at the relay that switches power to blower A. A fan motor draws more current than a module output can carry, so a relay is a natural choice: the module energises the coil (terminals 85/86 in HELLA's scheme) and the contact (30/87) feeds the motor.
s: Blower A dead, or running without command if contacts are welded
No relay click when cleaning is requested
Sensor cleaning warning with possible loss of assistance functions
c: Burnt or welded contacts in the blower A relay
Relay coil open or its control wire interrupted
Blown fuse or loose socket on the relay supply side

B0105.d: B0105 is the relay fault on the B side of the sensor-cleaning air supply. If B is a compressor rather than a small fan, as in Uber's patent where a compressor charges an accumulator and recharges once pressure drops to roughly 130–140 psi, the relay carries a sizable inrush current, and pitted contacts become the usual weak point.
s: Blower or compressor B does not start, or will not switch off
Droplets stay on sensor windows in rain
Assistance functions drop out when a sensor is reported blocked
c: Contacts of relay B pitted by high motor or compressor inrush current
Relay B coil or its suppression diode failed
Corroded relay socket or wrong relay type fitted

B0106.d: B0106 opens a row of four lidar washer actuators (A to D). The actuator is whatever delivers fluid to a lidar window: a washer pump or an electromagnetic valve.
s: No spray reaches lidar A during a cleaning cycle
Lidar blocked message and reduced automated driving availability
c: Washer pump or valve A for the lidar nozzle seized or electrically open
Wiring or plug fault at actuator A
Frozen washer fluid blocking pump A

B0107.d: B0107 is the second lidar washer actuator. Why a car would need several becomes clear in Uber's 2016 patent: its roof lidar is washed by three separate nozzle units, each with its own pump and check valve, fed from one reservoir, and the controller normally sprays fluid first and then dries with air.
s: One section of the lidar window stays dirty after washing
Repeated cleaning requests and lidar degraded warning
c: Washer pump B worn or its motor open
Check valve or line to nozzle B blocked, pump runs against closed path

B0108.d: B0108 covers lidar washer actuator C. Robotaxis with several lidars, for example on roof and corners, are where a third circuit would fit.
s: Lidar C not cleaned, especially in frost or snow
Automated driving refuses to engage or hands back control
c: Telescopic nozzle C stuck by ice or dirt, actuator overloaded
Distribution valve position C not switching
Nozzle heater or shared connector on circuit C faulty

B0109.d: B0109 ends the lidar washer group with actuator D; the next codes, B010A onward, move on to camera washers. Four lidar circuits match fleets built for driverless service: Kautex fits two complete Allegro cleaning and clearing systems to every Zoox robotaxi, combining water and air for cameras and lidars.
s: One lidar remains dirty while the other sensors are cleaned
Vehicle limits or ends automated driving
c: Pump or valve D for the fourth lidar nozzle defective
Hose to lidar D kinked or pulled off, so the actuator runs dry or overloaded
Open or shorted wire to actuator D

B010A.d: B010A opens a row of eighteen camera washer actuators, lettered A to S with I left out. The actuator is the electrically driven part that sends fluid to one camera lens: a pump of its own or a valve on a shared line.
s: The camera assigned to actuator A is no longer washed, neither on request nor automatically
Camera view stays dirty in rain, mud or road salt; a camera blocked message may appear
c: Valve coil or pump motor of actuator A open or shorted
Corroded or loose plug at actuator A, which sits in the splash zone near the camera
Driver stage in the controlling module defective

B010B.d: B010B covers actuator B. A common way to reach a reversing camera is a branch off the rear-window washer line with an electric switching valve.
s: In reverse the washer switch no longer sprays the reversing camera
Rear window may be washed instead of the camera, or neither
c: Coil of the rear-window/camera switching valve open or shorted
Broken wire in the tailgate or boot-lid harness passage to the valve
Reverse-gear signal that enables the camera wash not reaching the module

B010C.d: B010C names actuator C. Front cameras sit in the grille and get a jet of their own.
s: Front camera lens is not sprayed when the wash is requested
Front or 360-degree camera image stays dirty in winter or after off-road driving
c: Damaged wiring or plug at the front end, exposed to stone chips, water and salt
Pump or valve C seized or electrically defective
Plug left disconnected after grille or bumper work

B010D.d: B010D covers actuator D. Audi's TSB 2059228/2 (2022) for the 2019–2022 e-tron and 2020–2022 e-tron Sportback shows what a missing check valve does to a rear camera wash: the line empties while driving or when the tailgate opens, the system stops after four activations to save fluid, and four tries are not enough to refill and pressurise it, so the lens stays dirty until the ignition (terminal 15) is switched off and
s: Camera wash request must be repeated several times before fluid arrives, or nothing arrives
Reversing camera stays smeared after the wash function has been used
c: Pump or valve D open, shorted or drawing abnormal current
Wire break where the harness flexes into the tailgate
Pump damaged by repeatedly running dry on an empty line

B010E.d: B010E names actuator E, which may be a dedicated pump rather than a valve. Audi's TSB 2073568/1 (2024) for e-tron, e-tron S and Q8/SQ8 e-tron models reports rear camera washer pressure too low to clean the lens: the mono pump could not build enough pressure, and production moved to a dual pump (1K6 955 651) whose spare outlet is plugged.
s: Camera nozzle only dribbles; the spray does not reach across the lens
Pump hum without spray, or no pump sound at all when the wash is requested
c: Camera washer pump motor E worn, seized or open
Low supply voltage or poor ground at the pump
Clogged inlet filter making the pump labour and draw high current

B010F.d: B010F covers actuator F. On 2021 Chevrolet Tahoe and Suburban and GMC Yukon with the rear camera mirror (RPO DRZ), GM service update N202311260 found the hose feeding the rear camera nozzle kinked behind the tailgate trim in about 630 vehicles; technicians test the wash, shorten the hose to 127 mm at most and slide an 85 mm split sleeve over it.
s: Camera mirror or reversing image stays dirty because the rear camera wash does not work
Rearview image itself is still shown when reversing
c: Open or shorted circuit to valve or pump F
Wiring pinched or unplugged during tailgate trim removal

B0110.d: B0110 names actuator G. Not every washed camera sees visible light.
s: Night-vision or front camera image stays smeared; the camera jet does not spray
Assistance functions relying on that camera may report limited availability
c: Valve or pump G for the camera jet electrically open or shorted
Harness damage in the lower bumper area after a parking knock or repair
Output stage of the controlling module defective

B0111.d: B0111 is the J2012 code for camera washer actuator H, but the number has an older second life. Toyota's bulletin T-SB-0069-12 (revision 2, 2014) for the 2004–2009 Sienna lists B0111 together with B0116 as an open side-airbag squib circuit with the SRS lamp lit, repaired in the floor harness.
s: Camera served by actuator H is not washed
No washer fluid leaves the nozzle served by actuator H when the wash is requested
c: Pump or valve H open, shorted or seized
Water ingress or corrosion in the plug of actuator H

B0112.d: B0112 covers actuator J; the letter I is skipped in this row, so J is the ninth. Large systems wash many cameras from one fluid network.
s: One camera of a multi-camera system is not sprayed while others are
Damp trim or puddles of washer fluid inside the vehicle if a coupling has also come loose
c: Valve or pump J electrically open or shorted
Washer fluid from a loose coupling running into the actuator plug and corroding it
Chafed wire on the route to actuator J

B0113.d: B0113 names actuator K. Even a working actuator is useless if the jet misses the lens.
s: Camera wash does not run for the camera served by actuator K
Digital mirror or reversing picture stays dirty after the wash is requested
c: Open or short in the circuit of valve or pump K
Wire fatigue in the liftgate hinge area
Plug not reconnected after the camera or nozzle was removed

B0114.d: B0114 covers actuator L. Stellantis STAR case S2123000051 (2021, Jeep Grand Cherokee) describes a front camera washer pump that stopped spraying when the reservoir ran low although the cluster showed no low-fluid warning; a new pump, reservoir or level sensor did not help, and engineering was still investigating.
s: Camera wash stops working while the reservoir is low, without a low-fluid warning
Front camera view remains dirty after a wash request
c: Pump or actuator L damaged after running with a nearly empty reservoir
Open or shorted wiring to actuator L
Level sensor not warning in time, so the actuator runs without fluid

B0115.d: B0115 names actuator M. Where several cameras share one pump, the actuator is often a distribution valve.
s: One camera stays unwashed while other cameras on the same pump are sprayed
Camera blocked message for that camera in bad weather
c: Coil for outlet M in a shared valve block open or shorted
Valve M stuck by deposits or frozen fluid, drawing abnormal current
Wiring or plug fault on the line to valve M

B0116.d: B0116 covers actuator N. Like B0111 it also turns up on the 2004–2009 Toyota Sienna, where bulletin T-SB-0069-12 uses it for an open side-airbag squib circuit, not a washer.
s: Camera wash fails mainly in frost and recovers after the car has warmed up
Ice or salt film stays on the lens of the camera served by actuator N
c: Washer fluid without enough antifreeze frozen in pump or valve N
Actuator N electrically open or shorted

B0117.d: B0117 names actuator O; unlike I, the letter O is used in this row. Not every silent washer is faulty.
s: Camera stays unwashed also in normal road mode, not only when washing is intentionally paused
Camera blocked message in mud or rain
c: Valve or pump O open, shorted or seized
Wiring to a low-mounted camera actuator damaged by mud, water or off-road use
Module software or configuration fault in actuator O control; update per maker

B0118.d: B0118 covers actuator P. Equipment can disappear in the middle of a model year.
s: Fault stored although the camera has no working wash, or only a dummy jet without a hose
Camera image and parking aid otherwise work normally
c: Module coded for a camera washer actuator the vehicle is not built with
Actuator P or its feed open circuit
Replacement module fitted with the wrong variant data

B0119.d: B0119 names actuator Q. Land Rover's SSM76076 (2023) for the Defender (L663) from model year 2020 traces dripping headlamp washer jets and a dripping rear camera washer jet to a one-way valve in the feed pipe that no longer seals; the dealer tool runs a guided leak test and may call for a new rear camera washer hose with the valve.
s: Camera wash for the camera served by actuator Q does not respond
Washer fluid level drops faster than usual if a valve is also leaking
c: Pump or valve Q electrically open or shorted
Fluid dripping from a leaking jet or valve corroding the nearby actuator plug
Chafed wire between module and actuator Q

B011A.d: B011A covers actuator R. Some camera cleaners use air as well as fluid, so the actuator may be a blower as much as a pump.
s: Camera served by actuator R is neither blown nor sprayed clean
Drops or mud remain on the lens; assistance functions may warn of a blocked camera
c: Pump, valve or air blower R electrically open or shorted
Heater element in the camera wash circuit defective, affecting cold-weather operation

B011B.d: B011B closes the row with actuator S. Electrically, each actuator in the row is a coil or motor switched by a module or a relay.
s: Camera wash for the camera served by actuator S does nothing
Wash may run continuously or not stop if a relay contact has welded
c: Coil or motor of actuator S open or shorted
Relay feeding actuator S sticking or with a burnt contact
Blown fuse or broken supply wire to the relay or actuator

B011C.d: B011C is the first of six fluid reservoir level sensors, A to F. J2012 does not say which reservoir each letter belongs to; the neighbouring codes deal with washing windows, cameras and other sensors, so washer tanks are the obvious candidates.
s: Low-fluid warning stays on although the reservoir is full
No warning at all when the reservoir runs empty
c: Float jammed, rotated out of its guide or soaked with fluid
Reed contact inside the sensor broken or welded
Leaking grommet letting fluid reach the plug, corroded terminals

B011D.d: B011D concerns level sensor B. Not every washer tank relies on a float.
s: Warning lamp lit with a full reservoir, often after a change of washer fluid
Level warning appears late or not at all
c: Deposits from unsuitable washer fluid or additives on the sensing surface
Open or short in the sensor wiring

B011E.d: B011E covers level sensor C. Vehicles that steer by camera and lidar need their own cleaning supply, and there the level reading becomes an operating condition.
s: Refill request or cleaning-system warning without obvious reason
Sensor cleaning may be withheld, and assistance functions may restrict themselves when sensors get dirty
c: Level sensor C defective or signal implausible
Damaged wiring or connector between sensor and computing module
Dirt or ice in the reservoir disturbing the measurement

B011F.d: B011F reports level sensor D. A recurring weakness of float switches in washer bottles is motion: fluid slopping around in corners or under braking lifts and drops the float and can set it spinning.
s: Level warning switching on and off while driving, especially in bends
False low-level message with a full reservoir
c: Loose or corroded pins at an intermediate harness connector
Float moving freely with sloshing fluid, guide or slosh guard broken

B0120.d: B0120 relates to level sensor E. Ford's application US20190265715A1 describes a container for sensor cleaning whose level sensor measures conductance at a fixed height: air gives a resistance above roughly 1000 ohms, the slightly conductive fluid one below it.
s: Refill warning too early, too late or constantly on
Cleaning of exterior sensors may be restricted
c: Electrodes fouled or fluid with unsuitable conductivity (e.g. plain distilled water)
Open or short in the sensor circuit
Leaking reservoir or hose making the level drop unexpectedly

B0121.d: B0121 closes the row with level sensor F. Small local reservoirs are one reason a vehicle might carry six level sensors: Ford's application DE102018109892A1 describes a camera washer with its own container close to the lens, fitted with a buoyant level sensor that signals when the fluid has fallen to a set low point and the container needs topping up.
s: Missing or permanent refill message for the affected reservoir
Washer served by this reservoir runs dry without warning
c: Float of sensor F stuck by deposits or ice
Wiring to the small reservoir chafed or connector corroded

B0122.d: B0122 flags pedestrian alert speaker A. Hybrid and electric vehicles are almost silent at walking pace, so they have to make an artificial sound.
s: No artificial driving sound at low speed from the affected side
Warning message about the pedestrian alert system in the cluster, depending on make
Vehicle no longer meets the legal minimum sound; repair promptly
c: Speaker A failed from water, salt or stone impact at the front end
Open or short in the speaker wiring, often after bumper repairs
Output stage of the sound generator module or its fuse faulty

B0123.d: B0123 is the same check for pedestrian alert speaker B, which implies a second sounder. Ford's special service message 48451 for 2020 hybrids and plug-ins describes speakers at the front and the rear that sound in forward and reverse between 0 and 30 km/h.
s: Artificial sound missing at the front or rear, e.g. only audible when moving off forwards
Possible warning message about the pedestrian alert system
Legally required warning sound incomplete; have it repaired soon
c: Speaker B defective, for example from moisture in the rear bumper or wheel arch area
Loose or corroded connector at speaker B or a rattling internal connector at the module
Fault in the sound generator module or its software

B0124.d: B0124 points at the night vision camera, usually a far-infrared thermal sensor behind the grille or in the bumper; Teledyne FLIR says it has supplied more than a million automotive thermal sensors. Its exposed position causes most faults.
s: Night vision image missing, distorted or pixelated
Message such as night vision unavailable, service required
c: Water ingress through a stone-chipped or cracked camera window
Loose or corroded LVDS video connector between camera and control module
Camera replaced but not learned or calibrated

B0125.d: B0125 concerns the night vision control module, which processes the camera image and passes it to the display. Stellantis uses this code: on the 2023 Jeep Grand Cherokee the cluster stores B0125-02, Night Vision Control Module general signal failure, alongside U02BD (lost communication) in the BCM.
s: Night vision unavailable message in the cluster
No, frozen or pixelated night vision image
c: Misaligned, bent or not fully seated terminals at the module connector
Video link (LVDS) to the cluster loose or damaged
Camera delivers no usable image, e.g. cracked lens

B0126.d: B0126 belongs to the driver monitoring camera, an infrared camera aimed at the driver that tracks gaze and head position for hands-free and attention functions. GM uses the code: preliminary information PIC6556 (versions B to H, 2024–2025) for Super Cruise models from Cadillac Lyriq to Silverado EV lists B0126 symptom 82, stored by the module that processes camera images and often paired with B1DD0; the steps are a 3
s: Hands-free assistance such as Super Cruise unavailable or disengaging
Driver attention or distraction warning inactive, failure message shown
c: LVDS cable to the image processing module damaged or poorly connected
Software fault, or camera view blocked by objects or mounting problems

B0127.d: B0127 reports an open circuit to power outlet A of DC/AC converter A, one of the household-voltage sockets the converter supplies. Ford's patent US11043801B2, behind Pro Power Onboard, gives every socket its own conductor, on/off switch and ground-fault interrupter, fed by an inverter that draws on the traction battery, the motor-generator or both; sensors ahead of and behind each switch let the controller check the
s: Outlet A supplies no power while other outlets may still work
Message that onboard power or the outlet is unavailable
Outlet circuits carry 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised
c: Wire or terminal in the feed to outlet A broken or pushed out
Socket insert or its built-in protection defective
Output switch or relay for outlet A inside the converter faulty

B0128.d: B0128 is the open-circuit fault for outlet B. Such a fault has to be told apart from a tripped protective device.
s: Socket B dead, ground-fault or outlet message on the screen
Reset does not restore power to socket B
Outlet circuits carry 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised
c: Feed to outlet B interrupted at a connector or in the harness
Ground-fault interrupter of outlet B defective or its reset actuator stuck
Moisture or dirt in socket B

B0129.d: B0129 covers outlet C. Apart from wiring faults, the converter also cuts sockets on purpose when the load is too high.
s: Socket C stays dead even with no load connected
Outlet message that cannot be cleared by unplugging and resetting
Outlet circuits carry 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised
c: Terminal at outlet C overheated or burnt from heavy loads, contact lost
Switching element for outlet C inside the converter defective

B012A.d: B012A concerns outlet D. Sockets in a pickup bed live in a harsher place than those in the cab: dust, rain, washing and cords left plugged in.
s: Socket D without power, other sockets may work
Message that onboard power or an outlet is unavailable
Outlet circuits carry 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised
c: Water or corrosion in socket D or its connector, typical for exterior or bed outlets
Harness to outlet D chafed or crushed in the body or bed

B012B.d: B012B is the last outlet circuit code, for outlet E. Many trucks combine bed sockets with one in the cabin.
s: Socket E dead, possibly with a misleading breaker message for another outlet
Outlet circuits carry 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised
c: Connector at outlet E not fully engaged, e.g. after dash work
Circuit breaker of outlet E tripped or defective
Wiring between converter and outlet E open

B012C.d: B012C names power outlet control module A of converter A without a fault type, so the module itself is under suspicion rather than one socket. Ford calls its unit DCACA; on the F-150 with the 2.0 kW system it sits in the cab under the left rear seat.
s: Onboard power unavailable or service message in the centre display
Unusual fan noise from the module's location
Module handles 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised
c: Outdated or corrupted module software; reprogramming per maker bulletin
Power, ground or network connection of module A faulty
Module A internally defective, e.g. cooling fan or power stage

B012D.d: B012D addresses outlet control module B. A converter for household sockets interacts with the rest of the vehicle both electrically and by radio.
s: Outlets switch off or are unavailable
Side effects on radio-based systems such as tyre pressure monitoring
Module handles 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised
c: Supply voltage outside the permitted window, weak 12 V battery or poor ground
Module B overheating, blocked air path or cooling fan failed
Module B internally defective or emitting interference

B012E.d: B012E concerns outlet control module C. GM's name for the part is accessory AC and DC power control module: in program N222385490, 2023 Silverado and Sierra 1500 built from September 2022 without a working inverter, because of the chip shortage, received this module, a fuse and BCM reprogramming, with separate inverters for 110 V (RPO KI4) and 230 V (KI5).
s: Power outlets in cab and bed inoperative
Outlet functions missing from the display menu
Module handles 120/240 V AC from a high-voltage source; work only with the system de-energised
c: Module C or BCM not configured or programmed after installation or replacement
Fuse, supply or ground of module C faulty

B012F.d: B012F reports a fault in the control circuit for A/V sensor washer fluid A, the first of six such circuits, with B0130 to B0134 following. A/V most likely stands for autonomous vehicle; the circuit drives the pump or valve that delivers fluid to one sensor.
s: Sensor A is no longer washed, camera or lidar view stays dirty
Assistance or automated driving functions report sensor blocked or become unavailable
c: Pump motor or valve coil for fluid circuit A open or shorted
Damaged wiring or corroded connector in the control circuit
Driver stage in the controlling module defective

B0130.d: B0130 reports a fault where the module switches A/V sensor washer fluid B, the second of six channels running from B012F (A) to B0134 (F). A/V almost certainly stands for autonomous vehicle.
s: The camera or lidar on channel B stays dirty while the others are cleaned
Driver assistance or automated driving reports a blocked sensor or is withdrawn
c: Pump motor or valve coil on fluid channel B open or shorted
Corroded or loose connector at the pump, exposed to washer spray and road salt
Output stage for channel B in the controlling module failed

B0131.d: B0131 points to the circuit that switches A/V sensor washer fluid C, the third channel of the B012F to B0134 series for autonomous vehicle sensors. Ford's patent US10569746B2 describes a rotating sensor cover: the computer first tries a contactless cleaner with fluid or air and only brings in a wiper when the window's measured opacity stays above a limit.
s: Washing of sensor C stops; dirt, salt or insects stay on its window
A wiper or air jet, if fitted, has to do the cleaning alone
c: Pump or solenoid valve of channel C with open or shorted winding
Harness to the sensor cleaning unit chafed or pinched at a bracket
Controlling module output for channel C defective

B0132.d: B0132 concerns washer fluid channel D of a self-driving vehicle's sensor cleaning, the fourth in the series that starts at B012F. In Uber's patent US10173646B1 the vehicle computer judges how dirty each sensor is and then works out a cleaning order, so the cleaning units fire one after another instead of all at once; a dead channel removes one sensor from that rotation.
s: Sensor D is skipped in the cleaning sequence and stays dirty
Automated driving may limit itself or ask the driver to take over
c: Open circuit in the channel D pump or valve, often a burnt-out winding
Supply or control lead of channel D shorted to ground or battery voltage
Pump blocked by frozen or contaminated fluid, drawing excess current

B0133.d: B0133 covers the control circuit of A/V sensor washer fluid E, the fifth channel after B012F to B0132. Autonomous vehicles carry many cameras and lidar units, so cleaning is split into several separately switched fluid paths.
s: The sensor on channel E keeps a film of dirt or dried spray
Message that a sensor is blocked or an assistance function is unavailable
c: Pump or valve of channel E defective, coil open or shorted
Water ingress or corrosion in the connector of channel E
Output for channel E in the cleaning control module damaged

B0134.d: B0134 is the last of the six A/V sensor washer fluid circuits (B012F for A up to B0134 for F) and covers channel F. The module drives a pump or valve on this channel and reports the code when it finds an open or shorted output.
s: Sensor F no longer gets washer fluid; only air or a wiper, if present, still works
Assistance functions that rely on sensor F report reduced availability
c: Winding of the channel F pump or valve open or shorted
Wiring of channel F damaged, for example after bodywork near the sensor mount
Driver stage for channel F in the module failed

B0140.d: Neither the J2012 code lists available here nor any carmaker's public material contains B0140; its wording repeats B0061, the J2012 code for the front passenger belt tension sensor, and resembles B0182. The part itself is well described.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Passenger airbag status indicator may show an unexpected state
Safety note: the sensor sits near pretensioner and side airbag plugs; unplug only with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Loose or corroded plug at the passenger belt tension sensor
Sensor signal out of range, for example from a jammed slider
Sensor lead trapped under the seat or at the sill panel

B0150.d: No publicly available J2012 code list includes B0150, and no carmaker publishes it with this meaning. The mode door decides whether air leaves at the face vents, the footwell or the windscreen.
s: Air comes out of the wrong vents or the selected mode is not reached
Clicking or knocking behind the dashboard while the door moves
Windscreen demisting weaker because too little air reaches the defrost outlets
c: Mode door or its linkage binding, broken lever or stripped gear
Mode door actuator worn, feedback track of the potentiometer dirty
End positions not relearned after actuator replacement

B0152.d: B0152 appears in no J2012 code list and in no public carmaker document. In J2012 the driver's buckle sensor is B0050, so the title duplicates that code.
s: Belt reminder for the driver stays on or does not come on
Airbag warning lamp on in vehicles that read the buckle in the airbag module
Safety note: the buckle plug sits under the seat near airbag and pretensioner plugs; unplug only with the battery off and the wait time observed
c: Buckle plug under the driver seat loose or corroded
Buckle lead pinched or broken by seat movement
Hall sensor or contact in the buckle defective, buckle must be replaced

B0154.d: B0154 has no entry in the publicly available J2012 lists, and carmakers do not describe it in public material; J2012 assigns the front passenger buckle sensor to B0052, which this title duplicates. On the passenger side the buckle signal does more than drive a reminder: together with seat occupancy it helps the restraint module choose how the passenger airbag and pretensioner act.
s: Passenger belt reminder wrong, permanently on or missing
Airbag warning lamp on
Safety note: seat plugs share space with airbag and pretensioner wiring; disconnect the battery and wait before unplugging anything
c: Buckle connector under the passenger seat loose, corroded or kicked off
Buckle wire chafed by the seat rail or a seat adjustment
Switch inside the buckle worn or soiled by spilled drinks

B0156.d: The publicly available J2012 lists skip B0156, and public carmaker documents do not mention it; the same meaning is covered by code B0305. A sun load sensor on top of the dashboard tells automatic climate control how strongly sunlight heats the cabin, so the system can add cooling early.
s: Cabin gets too warm in strong sun because the system does not add cooling
Automatic blower and temperature react only to air temperature
c: Sensor plug under the dash top cover loose or damaged after windscreen work
Photodiode or electronics in the sun load sensor failed
Signal or supply wire shorted or open behind the dashboard

B0158.d: Although B0158 is absent from the publicly available J2012 lists, General Motors and Saab use it with exactly this meaning. In the 2011 Saab 9-4X the instrument cluster reads the outside air sensor and stores B0158 02 when the signal implies more than 88 °C, B0158 05 below −40 °C; the display then shows dashes.
s: Outside temperature display missing or showing dashes
Automatic climate control works with a stored or default temperature
On some GM models the HVAC display switches to Celsius
c: Sensor at the front bumper unplugged or connector damaged after front-end work
Thermistor in the outside air sensor open or shorted, often after stone impact
Signal or low reference wire to the cluster damaged

B0159.d: No public J2012 source lists B0159. General Motors uses it: bulletin PIP5094 from 2013 lists B0159 among its service information keywords, though without a description, so no public GM text states the exact fault logic.
s: Displayed outside temperature clearly too high or too low
Climate control or A/C compressor behaves oddly because of the wrong outside value
c: Outside air sensor drifted or slow to react, giving plausible but wrong values
Sensor mounted where engine or road heat reaches it, e.g. after a bumper repair
Corroded contact adding resistance and shifting the reading

B0160.d: B0160 is not among the publicly available J2012 entries, and no maker publishes it with this meaning; a similar title belongs to B0250. The in-car sensor tells automatic climate control the actual cabin temperature.
s: Automatic climate control overheats or overcools the cabin
Blower speed does not settle as the cabin reaches the set temperature
c: Thermistor in the in-car sensor open or shorted
Sensor plug behind the dash or headliner loose or corroded
Signal or reference wire damaged during interior work

B0162.d: No public carmaker source and no publicly available J2012 list covers B0162. The title implies a second sun load channel, as used for dual-zone climate control: Eaton's patent US5957375A describes a sensor that sees how much sun reaches separate areas of the cabin so each side can be cooled on its own.
s: One side of the cabin gets too warm in sun while the other is fine
Dual-zone automatic reacts to sunshine only on one side
c: Second photodiode or channel of a dual-zone sun sensor failed
Connector of the sensor in the dash top cover loose or damaged
Signal wire of the second channel open or shorted

B0164.d: B0164 is not listed in any publicly available J2012 table. General Motors does use the number: bulletin PIP5094 from 2013 lists it as a service information keyword, but no public GM text gives its wording.
s: Airbag or climate warning, depending on which module stored the code
Climate control may run on a substitute cabin temperature
Safety note: if the airbag module is involved, work only with the battery disconnected and the wait time observed
c: Temperature sensor or its wiring open or shorted
GM: fault in the climate control sensor group around B0163 rather than the airbag
Internal temperature measurement of the control module faulty

B0166.d: The public J2012 lists do not contain B0166, and no make describes it as a discharge air sensor. Saab does use it, for the cabin rather than the outlet: in 9-3 climate control manuals from 2003 to 2012, B0166 05 marks the indoor or compartment temperature sensor as open or shorted to supply once the module input rises above 4.8 V, checked continuously with the ignition on; B0165 02 is the matching short to ground.
s: Automatic climate control misjudges cabin or outlet temperature and over- or undercorrects
Set temperature is not held steadily
c: Sensor open or signal shorted to supply (Saab 9-3 cabin sensor)
Sensor connector loose or left unplugged after dashboard work
On other makes, the outlet duct sensor itself failed

B0168.d: B0168 shows up neither in the publicly available J2012 lists nor, with this meaning, in public carmaker documents; air mix door circuits have the codes B0258 and B0263. The air mix or blend door divides the airflow, sending part across the heater core and part past it, and so sets outlet temperature.
s: Outlet air stays hot or cold regardless of the temperature setting
Temperature swings or clicking behind the dash
c: Blend door shaft or lever broken or slipping on the actuator
Air mix actuator gear worn or motor weak
Foreign object or debris in the HVAC case blocking the door

B0170.d: Searching the available J2012 lists and public manufacturer material turned up no entry for B0170 with this title. Unlike B0150, which concerns how the mode door moves, this code points at the sensor that reports its position.
s: Air distribution stays fixed in one position
Actuator runs repeatedly or ticks after switching on
c: Worn or dirty potentiometer track inside the mode actuator
Feedback signal, 5 V supply or reference wire open or shorted
Bent or pushed-back pin in the actuator connector

B0173.d: B0173 lacks an entry in the public J2012 lists, but General Motors documents it clearly in its Global A climate control. In the 2011 Saab 9-5 and 9-4X manuals it covers the upper left duct air temperature sensor: B0173 02 when the signal is grounded, 05 for high voltage or an open; the module flags a signal under 0.1 V or over 4.9 V and continues with a default value.
s: Left vents too warm or too cold, or heating or cooling seems not to work
Climate control runs on a default duct temperature
c: Duct sensor harness pinched between HVAC case and cross-car beam (GM 17-NA-049)
Upper left duct sensor thermistor open or shorted
HVAC module calibration needing an update (GM PIT5383, 2015 models)

B0175.d: The J2012 tables at hand leave out B0175, and no maker ties it to the recirculation door; a recirculation door circuit has the code B0273. Saab assigns the number to a temperature sensor instead.
s: Recirculation cannot be switched or windows fog because the door stays on recirculate
Saab 9-3: left outlet temperature regulated less precisely
c: Recirculation door sticking or its actuator gear stripped
Saab 9-3: left vent air mix sensor or its lead shorted to ground
Actuator wiring or connector fault behind the glovebox

B0181.d: B0181 is missing from every publicly available J2012 code list, and no carmaker publishes it as a front blower code. Saab does use the number, for something else: its 9-3 climate control stores B0181 05 when the left floor air mix temperature sensor input rises above 4.8 V, i.e.
s: Front blower does not run at all or only at the highest stage
Windscreen demists slowly because almost no air reaches it
c: Speed command line between climate module and blower module open or chafed to ground
Blower control module or series resistor burnt out, often after a sluggish motor drew too much current
Blown fuse or melted connector in the blower power feed

B0182.d: B0182 appears in no J2012 list and in no public document of any carmaker, so the code cannot be verified. Its meaning overlaps B0061, the passenger belt tension sensor, and B0140.
s: Airbag warning lamp lit
Passenger airbag off indicator behaves unexpectedly with a child seat or adult in the seat
Safety note: airbag and pretensioner plugs are close by; disconnect the battery and wait before unplugging anything
c: Plug at the belt anchor sensor loose, corroded or pulled off when the seat was moved
Two-wire lead to the occupant detection module pinched or chafed under the seat
Sensor electronics faulty, for instance after a crash load on the belt

B0184.d: No publicly available J2012 list includes B0184, and no maker documents it as a rear blower code. In Saab's 9-3 climate control the number belongs to the solar sensor: B0184 06 means that circuit is open or shorted to ground, and the system then regulates as on an overcast day.
s: No airflow from the rear roof or floor vents
Rear seats stay warm in summer or cold in winter while the front is comfortable
c: Long harness run to the rear blower open or shorted, often at body joints or under trim
Auxiliary blower control module or rear resistor failed
Rear blower motor worn or blocked by debris drawn in through the rear intake

B0186.d: B0186 is not in the publicly available J2012 lists, and no manufacturer uses it for front blower speed. Saab assigns it to the solar sensor of the 9-3: B0186 01 is a short to B+ in that circuit, after which the climate control assumes cloudy weather.
s: Blower speed does not match the selected stage or fluctuates
Fan stops and restarts after a pause, sometimes with a grinding noise
c: Leaves or other debris drawn in through the air intake, braking or jamming the fan wheel
Worn blower motor bearings or brushes, motor runs slowly or stalls
Heavily clogged cabin filter loading the motor

B0188.d: B0188 cannot be traced: it appears in no publicly available J2012 list and in no public carmaker material. The rear wiper meaning repeats B0910, titled Wiper Motor Rear Circuit.
s: Rear wiper does not move or works only now and then
Rear wiper stops away from its rest position
c: Wires broken in the rubber boot between body and tailgate after years of opening
Corroded splice or connector in the rear wiper control circuit causing a voltage drop
Rear wiper motor seized, for example from a corroded spindle, or internally shorted

B0190.d: No known public source lists B0190, neither a J2012 table nor a carmaker document. The part named in the title is common: a cam on the wiper gear opens or closes contacts, so the control knows when the blades are at rest and can keep the motor running until they get there.
s: Wipers stop in the field of view instead of at the bottom of the screen
Wipers keep running after being switched off or intermittent mode fails
c: Park contacts in the wiper motor gear housing worn, dirty or corroded by water
Park signal wire or connector at the wiper motor open or shorted
Fuse or relay in the park supply circuit failed

B0192.d: B0192 is publicly unverifiable: it appears neither in a J2012 list nor in any carmaker's documents. A performance fault, unlike the circuit fault B0220, means the wiring may be fine while the wipers sweep too slowly or irregularly.
s: Wipers sweep noticeably slower than usual, especially on high speed
Wiper arms judder, hesitate or run out of step with each other
c: Wiper linkage pivots dry, corroded or binding, slowing the motor
Worn motor brushes or commutator, reduced torque and speed
Blades frozen to the glass or heavily loaded by snow
